# .github — agent rules

Repo-wide rules in root `CLAUDE.md`. Editing this file → Rule 0 there first (caveman ultra via `caveman:caveman` skill; skill missing = blocked).

Scope: CI workflows, runner policy, release pipeline, deprecating superseded versions.

## CI workflows — `.github/workflows/`

The next four rules are supply-chain security invariants, so they are written in full sentences on purpose (Rule 0 §4). Scorecard scores them (Pinned-Dependencies, Token-Permissions), and a violation is also a real attack surface.

- Every `uses:` reference is pinned to a full 40-character commit SHA followed by a comment naming the release, for example `uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # v7.0.1`. Never pin by tag or branch, and never call a reusable workflow by tag. Before writing a new SHA, confirm it with `gh api` against the tag, dereferencing annotated tags.
- Every workflow has a top-level `permissions: contents: read`. A write scope (`security-events`, `id-token`, `checks`, `pull-requests`) is granted only at job level, and only to the one job that needs it. Never grant a write scope at workflow level.
- No workflow runs `npm install`, `pip install` or `curl ... | bash`. Dependencies come from `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` or from a pinned action or image.
- Never put an expression such as `${{ github.event.* }}` inside a `run:` script, because event payload text is attacker-controlled. Pass it through `env:` and read the shell variable.

The runner policy is a security invariant too, so it is also written in full sentences.

- `release.yml` and `scorecard.yml` stay on GitHub-hosted runners (`ubuntu-24.04`) and never move to self-hosted. `release.yml` uses npm trusted publishing and the Sigstore provenance, which require a GitHub-hosted VM, and its `publish` job holds the OIDC token. `scorecard.yml` holds `id-token: write` and `security-events: write` and is kept hosted by owner policy. `ci.yml`, `qodana.yml`, `semgrep.yml` and `mutation.yml` use `runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64]`, the persistent organisation pool in the Default runner group, which is shared with other repositories and open to this public repository.
- The only gate between a fork's code and the pool machines is the repository setting `approval_policy: all_external_contributors`. Check it with `gh api repos/Axiumine/koa-utils/actions/permissions/fork-pr-contributor-approval` and never lower it. A fork can edit the workflow file it runs, so an `if:` guard inside a workflow is not a substitute. Never add a `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` trigger: both run with the base repository's token and secrets.
- Every listener started by a pool job binds to `127.0.0.1` on a port the operating system assigns, never on a fixed port, and no `docker run` publishes a port with `-p`. The only listener today is the in-memory mongod of the test suite. Its free-port probe is a brief wildcard bind before mongod starts, which cannot be removed without patching `mongodb-memory-server`.
- A green `Test coverage` or `qodana.yml` run now comes from the shared pool, so a compromised runner could report green without checking anything. `release.yml` rebuilds and re-tests on a GitHub-hosted runner, which bounds that, but its `verify` job still accepts the `qodana.yml` run as reported.

- Pool jobs: step `Isolate the Yarn cache to this job` set `YARN_CACHE_FOLDER=$RUNNER_TEMP/yarn-cache` → Yarn downloads not shared across jobs or repos (mongod binary + tool cache still persist on runner). Old `hooks:install` wrote `yarnlock-registry` filter into persistent workspace `.git/config` → later checkout smudge `yarn.lock` to `yarnproxy.gio.lan` → Hetzner runner (no LAN) fail `Fetching packages` with `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND yarnproxy.gio.lan` (PR 34). Filter gone from repo (mirror = opt-in `REGISTRY_MIRROR`, see `.githooks/CLAUDE.md`), but workspace that ran older commit keep config + smudged file, and Dependabot can write foreign host. So every pool job that run `yarn install` hold step `Use the public yarn.lock` (`uses: ./.github/actions/public-lockfile`) right before it: drop filter section, overwrite `yarn.lock` with raw blob (`git cat-file blob HEAD:yarn.lock`), fail if any `resolved` host ≠ `registry.npmjs.org`. Never `git checkout -- yarn.lock` for this: git skip file whose stat match index, smudged copy match → stay smudged. New pool job with `yarn install` → add the step. `corepack enable` after Setup Node → Yarn present on bare runner. Node 26 ship no Corepack (dropped in Node 25) → Node 26 job: Setup Node 24.14.0 → `corepack enable` → Setup Node 26.13.0 → step `Check the toolchain` assert `node -v` + `yarn -s node -v` = `v26.13.0` (`-s` mandatory: bare `yarn node -v` print 3 lines → compare always fail). Never `npm install -g corepack` (CI rule above). Assumed on runner: docker (user in group), git, python3, curl, libcurl4 + libssl3 (mongod).
- Pool offline → `Test coverage`, `qodana.yml`, release `verify` (needs green `qodana.yml`) all stall. Owner-only `--admin` bypass, only after local `yarn test:coverage` green.
- Job `Test coverage` (required check, name fixed) hold step `Static gates` = `yarn check:static`, before `yarn test:coverage`. Old `Coding standard` step folded in. Static gate → inside this job, never a new required context.
- Node pin in `ci.yml`: `Test coverage` = `24.14.0`, `Test coverage (Node 26.13.0)` = `26.13.0` → exact `engines` floors, never floating `24` / `26`. Widen/raise `engines` → both jobs + README + CONTRIBUTING + REPO + `docs/code/README.md` same change. Node 26 job not required until owner add it to ruleset. No `engines` widen before `yarn test:coverage` green on that Node.
- Docs-only PR skip: job `Scope` (`ci.yml`, `qodana.yml`) run `.github/actions/scope` → output `code`. `Test coverage`, `Test coverage (Node 26.13.0)`, `Qodana Ultimate Plus` hold `needs: scope` + job-level `if` → skipped job report pass for required check, names unchanged. Never `paths-ignore` / `paths:` on a workflow: path-skipped workflow report nothing → required check wait forever + `release.yml` `verify` find no `qodana.yml` run for SHA. `if` is fail-open: `needs.scope.result != 'success'` → run everything.
- `scope` allowlist `DOCS_ONLY` in `.github/actions/scope/action.yml`: `*.md`, `docs/`, `LICENSE`, `CODEOWNERS`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/`. Everything else = code → full CI. Allowlist not denylist: new config file runs CI by default. Only `pull_request` events skip; push to `main`, schedule, dispatch always run all. `Trivy`, `SAST`, `Dependency audit` never skipped (cheap, a secret can sit in a `.md`). Widen allowlist → test with a throwaway repo (rename `src/x.mts` → `docs/x.md` must stay `code=true`: `--no-renames`).
- Advisory jobs, not required checks: `Trivy` (digest-pinned image, `--exit-code 1`; ghcr rate limit → red = rerun first), `Leak check` (schedule/dispatch only), `mutation.yml` (weekly Sun 03:43 UTC + dispatch, 120 min). Never hook, never required without ruleset edit. Semgrep registry packs (`--registry`) = CI `semgrep.yml` only, never hook, never `release.yml`.
- YAML in `.github/` = 2 spaces, overrides `.editorconfig` tabs (tab invalid in YAML).
- `qodana-action` bump (hand or Dependabot) travels with `qodana.yaml` `linter:` and `--linter` arg in `qodana.yml` → all same version, else CI + hook scan different images. Dependabot cannot bump the two → check by hand.
- `SEMGREP_IMAGE` (tag + `@sha256` digest) identical in `semgrep.yml` and `release.yml`. Change both same commit.

## Release pipeline — `.github/workflows/release.yml`

Owner only. Agent never trigger it, see *Never* in root `CLAUDE.md`.

- Trigger: owner publish GitHub release `vX.Y.Z`. `workflow_dispatch` = dry run, `verify` job only. Never add `push` / `pull_request` / `schedule` trigger.
- `verify`: tag == `v` + `package.json` `version`; stable `x.y.z`; tag commit ∈ `origin/main`; version absent on npm; green `qodana.yml` run for SHA; `yarn test:coverage`; semgrep canary + scan; `yarn build`; `npm pack --ignore-scripts`; tarball allowlist `dist/` `LICENSE` `README.md` `package.json`, 0 `.map`.
- `publish`: env `npm-publish` (reviewer = owner, tag rule `v*`; create BEFORE npm trusted publisher + first release, see invariants below), OIDC trusted publishing, provenance. `release-assets`: `actions/attest-build-provenance` → upload `<tgz>.intoto.jsonl` + `<tgz>` to the release.
- Why `.intoto.jsonl`: Scorecard Signed-Releases = 10 only if each of 5 newest releases-with-assets carry asset ending `.intoto.jsonl`. Name check only, content unread. `.sig` / `.sigstore.json` = 8 max.
- Consumer verify: `gh attestation verify <tgz> --bundle <tgz>.intoto.jsonl --repo Axiumine/koa-utils` → `docs/verify-release.md`. `slsa-verifier` not read this format.
- Release order (owner): bump `version` + `CHANGELOG.md` + `docs/code/README.md` (+ `SECURITY.md` table on major) → merge `main` → wait green `qodana.yml` → push signed tag `vX.Y.Z` → `gh release create vX.Y.Z --verify-tag --notes-file <file>` → approve `npm-publish` → run green → `npm view` + `gh attestation verify`. Release target = `main`, never a `release/*` branch.
- Version published via `yarn upload` → no GitHub release for it: `release.yml` would fail its npm guard.

Security invariants of `release.yml`, written in full sentences on purpose. The `publish` job holds the npm OIDC token, so it must never check out the repository and must never install dependencies; it only publishes the tarball that `verify` built and tested, after re-checking its sha256. Every action in the workflow is pinned by full commit SHA with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment and never by tag. The workflow never stores an npm token: authentication is OIDC trusted publishing only, bound on npmjs.com to the file name `release.yml` and the environment `npm-publish`, so renaming either one breaks publishing until the trusted publisher is recreated. The environment `npm-publish` must keep its required reviewer and its tag-only deployment rule, otherwise a branch carrying an edited copy of the workflow could request the OIDC token. The environment `npm-publish` must therefore exist, with the required reviewer and the `v*` tag-only deployment rule already set, before the npm trusted publisher is configured and before the first release is cut: GitHub silently creates a referenced but missing environment on the first run with no reviewer and no tag rule, which removes that guarantee. Check with `gh api repos/Axiumine/koa-utils/environments`; an empty list means the environment does not exist yet. The `registry-url` of the `publish` job stays `https://registry.npmjs.org` without a trailing slash, because Scorecard's Packaging check compares that exact string. GitHub immutable releases must stay disabled, because the assets are attached after the release is published and an immutable release would reject them. A GitHub release is created only to publish a new version through this workflow, because the workflow is what attaches the `.intoto.jsonl` provenance asset. A release that holds assets but no `.intoto.jsonl` scores 0 on Signed-Releases, so never attach, replace or delete release assets by hand. Never back-fill releases for old tags, and never create a release for an already published version: it starts the workflow, which then fails its guard. The trusted publisher on npmjs.com must grant the `npm publish` permission, not only `npm stage publish`: with no trusted publisher the `Publish` step fails with `404 Not Found - PUT`, and with `stage publish` alone it fails with `403 OIDC permission denied for this action`. Create it in the npmjs.com web UI (package Settings, Trusted Publisher, GitHub Actions: owner `Axiumine`, repository `koa-utils`, workflow `release.yml`, environment `npm-publish`, permission `npm publish`), or with `npm trust github @axiumine/koa-utils --repo Axiumine/koa-utils --file release.yml --env npm-publish --allow-publish`. The CLI answers 403 when the logged-in token is a granular token that bypasses 2FA, so use the web UI or a fresh `npm login` session. A failed `Publish` step is retried with `gh run rerun <id> --failed` once the trusted publisher is fixed, and the owner approves `npm-publish` again.

## Deprecating superseded versions

Broken version stay installable forever via exact pin or stale lockfile. Semver range carry nobody forward — `^5.0.0` only help consumers who re-resolve. `npm deprecate` = only channel reaching a pinned install. **Bump `version` for a fix → ask whether superseded version need deprecating. Raise with owner before publishing.**

- Deprecate on real defect: auth bypass, enumeration oracle, data corruption, swallowed error, wrong HTTP status, broken artefact. Rule of thumb — anything earning `### Security` or `### Fixed` in `CHANGELOG.md` that change observable behaviour.
- **Never blanket-deprecate merely-old versions.** Deprecation mean "this version bad", not "not newest". Blanket → consumers ignore warning, and it fire in CI for every lockfile pin — exactly the audience needing the signal for a real defect. No published version stay undeprecated as of 6.0.0: the introspection env gate gave every version `<= 5.9.0` a real defect, so all 19 carry a message. Still not a blanket — 9 tiers, each name its own defect class, each keep the older defect it already named. (`5.7.2` / `5.8.0` were this rule's worked example until 6.0.0 gave them a defect too → both deprecated now, so the example is currently empty. Example go stale each release — read npm, never this line: `npm view '@axiumine/koa-utils@>=4' deprecated --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/`.)
- Owner ask only, same standing as `yarn upload`. Read `CHANGELOG.md` first for the real cutoff per defect — "fixed in 5.4.0" → every version `<= 5.3.0` carry it. Never guess range off version numbers.
- 1 command per defect class, not 1 blanket range. Message name the defect + the fixed version — that string is all a consumer see at install time. Tier ranges when reasons differ; message vague enough to cover everything = message nobody act on.
- Pin registry, same reason as `yarn upload`:
  ```
  npm deprecate '@axiumine/koa-utils@<=5.3.0' "Security: <what breaks>. Upgrade to <fixed>. See CHANGELOG <version>." --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
  ```
- Verify: `npm view '@axiumine/koa-utils@>=4' deprecated --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/`. Propagation lag → immediate read-back can come back empty. Retry before concluding command failed. Reversible: same command, empty message (`""`).
- Nothing in repo record a deprecation. `CHANGELOG.md` = source of truth for *why* → message quote it, not restate it.
